utterances.text: Is it true that it happened more than once?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So it happened to you several times that you would head out to go somewhere and then reach a completely different destination without knowing how you got there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was probably immersed in my thoughts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: This can be seen in the expert report. Exhibit 2D127, page 6. And for the sake of the speed, and the witness has confirmed this, could this be admitted into evidence, Dr. Dzigurski expert report.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not an expert report by Dr. Dzigurski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Maybe I made a mistake. I apologise. I see that it says here forensic expert, Dr. Slavica Dzigurski, neuropsychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not referring to the expert report. The expert report was produced by the occupational medicine institute, and it should have been signed by Professor Bulat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have we had 2D127 on the screen? You are referring to a document we haven't seen, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I thought that it appeared on the screen. This is also not a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Please look at the first page. Municipal court in Pancevo. Expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then can we see the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Forensic expert Dr. Slavica Dzigurski, neuropsychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an expert report. She is a forensic expert, but the document that is used for forensic expertise --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you. I agree, it doesn't need to be an expert report. Is it an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I never saw that document. I believe that it is authentic, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Did you talk to Dr. Dzigurski?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she examined me. She's a forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Were you examined in relation to your complaints concerning which you sued Petrohemija?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in that case Slavica Dzigurski was appointed forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is sufficient. The time flies. So can this document also be admitted into evidence. This is 2D127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D63 marked for identification under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another document, the last document. This is a public complaint. It's a complaint filed with the court. It's a public document, 2D123. I don't know whether we should broadcast it or not. This is a complaint filed by the lawyer of Mr. Sliskovic in the Pancevo court in his case against Petrohemija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is publicly filed, I don't think that there's a specific reason not to show it to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that as your lawyer was drafting this complaint, you gave him documents and you told him - and this can be found in paragraph 3 in the middle - that there was a significant deterioration of your mental health and that you had the following diagnosis: F45, A41, and F06, which are well known in psychiatry?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My lawyer is not an expert in medicine. As for the F06 diagnosis, that was a diagnosis in observation, and I don't know what the neuropsychiatrist concluded because the court case is not over yet. There has been no judgement, either in my favour or in the favour of the other party. My lawyer considered it important to mention these diagnoses in the complaint. And based on everything that happened, it was established that my work ability was affected, as a result of which I worked as a security officer in Pancevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I want this complaint to be admitted into evidence as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification so as to give an opportunity to the parties to further discuss the relevance and other relevant considerations for admission into evidence. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D64 marked for identification -- under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think this doesn't have to be under seal. Mr. Bakrac, does it? You said it was publicly filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there are no problems. It was publicly filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D64 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now see 2D126.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Do you recognise your medical file, your medical history, dated 19 July 2006?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether you recognise your medical history.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Could we now see page 2 where it says CNS. I will read out what it says. And will you please confirm that this is the doctor's finding. It says here: "Anxious, depressed, sleeps poorly, has nightmares, has sudden mood changes, fear of being in closed area, has paranoid ideas (conspiracy theory after using Ksalol in the morning)."

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the doctor wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So you agree with me that this was written by a doctor?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we tender this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was my health condition after I was exposed to toxic substances, mercury.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the document for -- the number for the document which will be marked for identification is ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D65 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, D65, MFI'd. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, another document, due to the fact that the witness denied some things from his complaint, and this should not be publicly broadcast. This is an expert report, 2D125. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Could the witness verify the diagnosis. Are you familiar with this expert report?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Do you see here diagnoses F41 and F45 as your diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not F06.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: We will get to that, sir. Tell me, please, sir, can you see in the middle it says occasional loss of determinate tendency in the thought process?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was written by doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this was written by doctors, that's why I'm asking you whether this was your document which was drafted after you were examined by doctors.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will are marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D66 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like now to turn to the statement. I don't have much time left, so I will start immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, today you said in examination-in-chief that you left the so-called JATD after Pauk operation and that you tried to ask to be released immediately after the Pauk operation concluded?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Tara I wrote a request asking to be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Did you give this request to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was written in one copy only, and I gave it to Zvezdan Jovanovic at the Mount Tara camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And you did not want to be a member of the SDB unit any longer?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote, that I no longer wanted to be a member of the unit or of the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have P442 here, and we need page 4. This is a certificate on the years of service of Mr. Sliskovic where we can see that he worked for exactly one year and not a single day more or less, not a single month more or less, from what his contract stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Is that true, Mr. Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is when the decision on my status was annulled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Sir, how is it possible that you wrote your request asking to be released from the unit on the day when the decision assigning you to that unit expired?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I wrote it on the same day. Simply I was at the Tara camp when I wrote this request. Then I spent some time in Belgrade and I came back several days later and Milenko left the unit together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness, I put to you that your work contract expired. You had a one-year work contract and that you had to leave the state security and that as a result of that you have a grudge?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the record, because I don't have time to go back, diagnosis F06 can be found in Exhibit 2D127 on page 4 under item 7. I owed you that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you assist us in what exhibit number that received?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's D63 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness, so after the Operation Pauk, you no longer wanted to be a member of the state security?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I wrote that statement, that's how I felt and that's how I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: No, I withdraw this question. My question is as follows: Is it true that after the 72nd Brigade when you were discharged from there you signed up for the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. I signed up for the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Sir, if it's true that the Serbian Volunteer Guard was under the jurisdiction of the state security of Serbia, why did you then go to a unit that was under the Serbian DB when you no longer wanted to be a member?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that I no longer wanted to be a member of the unit, I was referring to the unit led by Zvezdan Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: But a bit earlier you said that you no longer wanted to be a member of a DB unit, not a unit led by Zvezdan Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I expressed myself inaccurately. When I wrote the request to leave the unit, the reason was because the deputy Zvezdan Jovanovic at the camp forced me to stand guard for eight to ten hours every day --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: You've already told us that. We don't need to hear it again. Witness, is it true that before joining the DB in May of 1994 you had a contract with the army, a three-year contract with the army?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a contract with the army. I don't know for what period of time. But when I was supposed to start working here, I was told to write a statement saying that for personal reasons I wanted to leave the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So you terminated your work contract with the army, lying to them that it was for personal reasons, and not telling them that it was because you were hired by state security?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wrote that reason down because I had been told that I shouldn't write the real reason to the army. That's what I was told by the state security, and I did as I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated that in the 72nd Brigade you were not allowed to join that brigade because you had been a member the state security?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did become a member of the 72nd Brigade. I spent a certain amount of time there. And the commander who was my commander at the time, I think his name was Zivkovic, told me that he no longer wanted me to be a member of the 72nd Brigade because I had been a member of this other unit. And he sent me to Avala to give back my equipment. And he actually wanted me to meet with the security officer who interrogated me about the Pauk operation in Western Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Did you state this to the OTP investigator that that was the reason you left the 72nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: While you were a member of the at the 72nd Brigade, did you confiscate a weapon from somebody?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't confiscate any rifle from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see Exhibit P440, which is the first statement of this witness. Paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: We don't have much time, so I will read it out to you: "I confiscated a rifle from a 13-year-old boy, and I told him to tell his father to go back to the MUP to get it back." While you were a member of the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a bad translation. It was a pistol, 7.62 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And who did you confiscate it from?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This boy's name was Nenad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And what authority did you have to confiscate weapons from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an authorised official entitled to confiscate weapons, but due to the boy's security, I thought it was better if I confiscated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Did you surrender it to the police, or were you later accused for doing that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't surrender it to the police, but I told this boy to send the owner of the weapon to the police to come and get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And did he come?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't because later it turned out that it was a weapon owned by a railway worker who had been killed at the railway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And how did this emerge? When the police got involved?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police told me what this was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Yesterday you said that when you were in Petrova Gora -- first of all, let me ask you this: How many times did you see Legija in Petrova Gora? How many times did he enter that room that was, according to you, used by Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was standing guard, we rotated. I saw Legija at least three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: How many times did you hear that Legija said, or rather, requested and said, I'm going to attack Kladusa from the front side; how many times did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that through an open window. I was standing guard, and I heard Legija saying that once. He wanted to carry out a frontal attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So that happened just once? He requested to be in charge of a frontal attack against Kladusa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How possibly do you think that the interpreters can follow this speed of speech? Please try to make pauses and try to speak at a decent speed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So we have agreed that you heard Legija only once when he said that he would carry out a frontal attack against Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Is it true that on direct examination you said that Franko Simatovic responded to him, "Act according to plan"?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he said things, "Will happen according to our agreement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Could you please look at P440, paragraph 8. And just for the time restrictions I'm going to start reading before it appears on the screen. And starting in the middle, there was a meeting at the staff, and so on and so forth: "We did not dare eavesdrop on their conversations, however it so happened that I heard them use the term 'Pauk,' and I also heard Legija (whose deputy was Sarac), and I don't know his name, Legija requested for an approval to attack the Velika Kladusa. I also heard Abdic who told him that that should be a classical infantry attack and that he did not want a single building to be destroyed in that attack." Witness, I'm putting it to you that you made everything up, because in your statement you stated that that Abdic responded to Legija's request.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, I stated things as I remember them. I never attempted to learn my statement by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So what do you remember? Was it Franko Simatovic or Abdic who responded to Legija's words?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm now sure that it was Franko Simatovic and nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So now your memory is much fresher than it was when you provided your statement in September 2003; right? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I remembered some things after providing the statement at a later stage. As simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's no answer in the transcript. This is what I've just been suggested by my colleague, or rather, what I'm being told is that there's no separation between my question and my answer, but this will probably be done at a later stage. Let's not waste time on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness, in 2003 your statement was different. Today in 2010 your statement is again different. Are you saying that your memory is fresher and that you remember better today than you did in 2003 and the events happened in 1994?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that I remember better. When I provided my statement, I was speaking from memory. I did not learn any of my statements by heart. I simply said what I remembered at the time, what came to mind first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Zika Crnogorac was with you in the convoy when you were headed for Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in the same bus with my group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: What was Zika Crnogorac's name?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that his family name was Ivanovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: When did you learn that his family name was Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that -- or rather, I knew his family name, but I'm not sure, so I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: When did you learn that his family name was Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe five or six years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Five or six years ago. Could you please look at your statement provided in 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the number is P441, and the paragraph that I'm interested in is 87, which is on page 31 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: You said a month ago: I can recognise that on the basis of the name of Darko Coklin's, which is Zika Crnogorac's name.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Coklin was the lad who was sitting next to me on the bus, and Zika Crnogorac, when we crossed the border there was -- we stalled, and he called Coklin to get off the bus and to come to urgently while he was hiding in the corn fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Witness, I have to finish within the next three minutes. There are major discrepancies here, and let me finish with the following question: Your observation, therefore, that Arkan's Volunteer Guard was under the DB is, first of all, as the way I understood it, is that the guards in front of the house were armed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Could security be provided by the army, the General Staff, or anybody else during the war?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with the man who worked in the security in front of Bogdan Ljutice's house. He is Montenegrin. Ljutice is his name. And not for a single moment did he mention that either the army or anybody else provided security. The lad didn't even know who provided security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: So don't tell me something that you don't know. He said that you didn't know who provided security. I'm asking you this: Was it the military security that could have been put around that house or maybe the public security sector? Who could have allowed the armed guards in front of the party headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was impossible under the law to stand guard with automatic weapons unless it was done by a regular formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Could a guard be stood with a pistol?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you. You are saying that they drove through Serbia in their vehicles and they were armed. When did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the staff of the Party of Serbian Unity and the driver came to pick me up and in his van he had an automatic rifle and he was wearing a uniform with insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: And he drove you to the front line?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: I know, first you dropped by Stara Pazova and then you went to Erdut to the front line?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. We went to Erdut finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Was there a war going on?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that a war was going on there; I said that there was a camp there which was used by the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Were people armed there?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's conclude my cross-examination, Witness. As a matter of fact you only speculate. You don't have exact and proper information as to what the link was between Arkan's volunteers and the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke from my personal experience and the time that I had spent with those people there based on what I heard at the staff of the Serbian Volunteer Guards and from their members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: What did you hear, the staff of the Serbian Volunteer Guard? You never told us anything about that. I read to you what you actually stated in your statement and how you reached your conclusions, now you are giving us a completely new information. What did you hear there in the staff of the Serbian Volunteers Guard?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to Erdut and more specifically about the money that arrived. They told us that the money had arrived from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Who told you that the money arrived from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that his name was Captain Lada [phoen]. He was in charge of the camp when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Did he also tell you where from Serbia was the money sent?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Thank you very much. I have no further questions for you. Your Honours, I hope that I have delivered on my promise and that I finished within the 50 minutes just as I promised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we give 60 seconds for everyone to recover from transcribing, translating at a speed -- and if gives me an opportunity to express my great admiration for your performance. Mr. Weber, how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe I can finish by 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sliskovic, on page T5161 of yesterday's transcript, you were asked questions about insignias that were worn by different armed forces that had red berets. You yourself have testified that you were a member of the regular formation of the JATD. Could you please describe whether or not there were the same or different insignias also worn by the reserve paramilitary units of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some wore the same insignia, and some appeared wearing insignia that differed from ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please mention these different insignias, and if you could briefly describe them?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvezdan Jovanovic, for example, wore a different insignia. He had an eagle on his flak jacket. And that was the first time I saw an insignia of that kind. There was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the description of the insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the description you gave from the insignia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It looked like the insignia that was later on worn by Special Police Units. It was a wolf on a copper shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday you adjusted your cap in a particular way when it was provided to you by Mr. Knoops. Where did you learn to adjust your cap in the manner that you did?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the cap is concerned, at the Lipovica forest camp I was told how to put it on, how to attach the insignia on the beret, and it's not done in the same way in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the way that you put it on yesterday, was it the way that you wore it while you were a member of the JATD or a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I wore it when I was a member of the JATD.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution did create a photo still of yesterday's proceedings. At this time we tender what we've marked as 65 ter 5318. It is a still of the witness wearing the beret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar, the exhibit number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P487 is admitted into evidence. Perhaps we could have a look at it on the screen so that we know what is admitted evidence. Meanwhile, please proceed so that we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in order to proceed, I have to go to a new exhibit, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Well, I see it on some screens close to me. Please proceed with your next exhibit, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Today you were also asked a number of questions about the command structure in Pauk and also tactical groups. You were shown certain selected excerpts from Exhibit P235 which is a diary from Pauk. I do not have time to go through all the different examples in this diary, however, I would like to use one example before we conclude today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 53 of the English version and page 73 of the B/C/S version of Exhibit P235 in evidence. We'll be referring to the entry at 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the exhibit in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The entry at 1900 hours states: "Legija arrives personally and reports that he took part at Prokresa and Dzaferovica Brdo. Pauk and commanders of TG-2 and TG-3 are going to a briefing at Frenki's." My question to you is: Do you know who the Frenki is that's being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And do you know the reason why Franko Simatovic went by the nickname of Frenki?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was in charge of the Serbian Volunteers Guard and the tactical group that was headed by the Radojica Raja Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that was not the question, and I don't know -- and I don't see what part of my cross-examination does this arise from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One, it arises from the cross-examination of the Stanisic Defence; two, I was just about to re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But then, Your Honours, by your leave, the Prosecutor can then take the diary because Stanisic's Defence used the diary and can raise thousands of new issues from that diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question has been put, the question has been answered. You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know why Franko Simatovic went by the nickname of Frenki?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that Franko Simatovic took his nickname while he was still in Knin in the 1990s. People said that it was a Croatian name and that Simatovic took this nickname Frenki from the proper name Franko.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Has the re-examination triggered any need for further questions? The Chamber has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have three short additional questions in terms of the re-examination. Further Cross-examination Mr. Knoops:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First question: Mr. Witness, what happened with your red beret of the 72nd Special Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned the entire equipment, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You just told us that there is a different way to put on the red beret within the army; is that correct? Could you -- can the red beret once more be given to the witness, and could the witness show us the difference between how the red beret was worn at the --

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can -- even without putting the beret on, if you want me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: It's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you briefly answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. While I worked at the 1205 military post, I was told that the insignia emblem should be in the middle of the forehead. As for the emblem that you can see here, it was supposed to be at the end of the left eye. So, towards the left side. As for the 72nd Brigade, the emblem was supposed to be right in the middle of an eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Last question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it right in the middle of the eyes, or is it -- could you choose which eye? I mean we are talking --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. The beret was on the left side, from the left to the right. And in the 72nd Brigade, the emblem was supposed to be in the middle of the left eye. I didn't have a mirror when I was putting it on here, but I was told that it was supposed to be at the end of the left eye. On this side here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a total puzzle for me. Could the witness put it on as he did it in the 72nd so that we can compare the pictures. Would you put it on in the way that you did it in the 72nd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the beret was turned to the same side. The emblem was supposed to be in the middle. I don't have a mirror in front of me. I am not sure that I will do it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the camera, I believe, is on the Bench and not the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we have six cameras, so I take it that we have -- all the camera recordings are kept, so it's always possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I put it for -- in such a way that the middle of the emblem is right above the middle of the left eye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whereas for the JATD it was just slightly a couple of centimetres more to the outer side of that eye. It's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- has it been on the video finally? I take it it has. Yes. So you can choose whatever still you want, Mr. Weber. Please proceed, Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you confirm that the briefing which was referred to by the Prosecution in the Pauk diary was briefing on intelligence, in other words, Mr. Simatovic was giving intelligence information to some of the people mentioned in that diary?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what kind of information he received. I can only give you my assumptions. But I don't know the facts, since I did not attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no knowledge about the entry we just looked at as to what the briefing was about; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You have now clarified for us that you don't know whether the information that Mr. Simatovic received at the time were intelligence information or not. Is it true that at Magarcevac where you stood guard and where Mr. Simatovic was there was a centre where they collected, gathered information, from 30 different wire-tapping intercepting centres?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Signalsmen came in with reports, and I was present when a signalsman came into a meeting and said that a report from Pljesevica was late. I know that there were communications centre, but I wasn't sure whether these were typical classical communications centre or something else. Because on two occasions, I spoke, using the code list, with some other places, but I didn't know what kind of other places they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you were present on one occasion when an intelligence report was laid, was being delayed. It was being delayed for whom, for Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN SLISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the signalsman came in and he said to Mr. Simatovic at that meeting that a report from Pljesevica was delayed. Was late. I don't know whether it was an intelligence report or some other kind of a situation report or anything else that was being late.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. You have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will use another couple of seconds to apologise to the interpreters and court reporters. I wanted to be of assistance so that we can finish with this witness today. And I apologise to you also for the speed of my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it that there is some understanding among the interpreters and transcribers. Mr. Sliskovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the Bench and by the parties. We will adjourn. And there is still a matter to be discussed among the parties with the Bench about Tuesday. Now, in view of the estimates of time given by the parties, the Chamber thought that we could deal with some procedural matters today in the last 45 minutes. That turned out not to be possible. The Chamber is considering to have a housekeeping session on Tuesday. That would be -- let me just have a look. That would be Tuesday, the 25th of May, at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, but the Chamber will be further in contact with the parties about whether or not we'll have that meeting, whether there's any other way of hearing evidence on that day because that's a matter still to be discussed. I also sincerely apologise with the interpreters, transcribers, and all those who are assisting us. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
